digest.component_or_area: completion-verifier epic-close gate and LLM integration
propositions: The epic-close bug screen converts LLMUnavailableError from per-candidate LLM provider failures into degrade-to-C verdicts, silently blinding the caused_by bug floor when the provider is degraded or misconfigured.

When max_tokens cap is set for a larger model (128K) and then the request is routed to a smaller model (64K haiku), the cap is never re-clamped, causing a Bedrock ValidationException 400 on every per-candidate screen call.

LLMUnavailableError and its subclass LLMConfigError must propagate (not degrade) from epic_bug_screen to the close gate's fail-closed handler to block the close with a clear error, consistent with the absent-provider path.
Non-provider per-candidate failures (malformed output, store errors) must continue to degrade to C verdict; the re-raise predicate is isinstance-based catch of LLMUnavailableError only.

The completion-verifier run succeeded and emitted PASS verdict with signed attestation withheld from the epic close due to two uncertified descendants (tickets 0059, 2bc7), which is intended behavior per gate design, not a defect.
